Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. The engine (lib/island/, registry item island-core): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only.

new.description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
new.readme: tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser. Small: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included. Fast: about 70x real time on four CPU threads. Two voices: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz. Runs anywhere: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web. Open: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch. Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.

new.description: Yab, yet another browser: a fast native macOS browser with an iPhone and Android companion
new.readme: Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone. Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page. One field takes addresses and searches. Pages run on WebKit, the engine inside every Mac, or, on Apple silicon, on Chromium, per tab or per site. Agents from the AI providers you already pay for can work in tabs of their own, and never see a private tab. One field. Type an address and you go there; type words and you search.

new.description: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
new.readme: a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics PEAR is a post-training engine for agentic robotics: it trains reasoning models to natively use robots, with reinforcement learning in simulation. PEAR is the training infrastructure behind Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots, where an open 27B reasoning model learns to use real robots entirely in simulation, with zero demonstrations.

items.connection: The OpenCode LoRA lifts local Qwen3.8-27B at about one eighth the tokens, Spark Attic frees about 2 GB more KV cache on headless DGX Sparks, and DSpine speeds the same base model, so each box can carry more concurrent agent sessions.
items.context: many client contracts forbid sending code to third-party APIs
chain: The LoRA lifts SWE-bench Pro Hard 51 from 35.3% to 51.0% with thinking off and about one eighth the tokens.
Fewer tokens per task and about 2 GB more KV cache let one headless Spark hold more parallel sessions or longer repo context.
DSpine reports 2.3x to 3.2x throughput on agent replays for the same base model, if its drafts still match the adapted outputs.
A consultancy can price private agent seats per box instead of per developer workstation, which makes on-prem coding agents viable for small teams.
items.who: Software consultancies and agencies working on restricted client code benefit; they pay for Spark hardware and setup time.
items.versus: Cloud coding agents are ruled out by NDAs, and a base model without the adapter solves fewer tasks while burning more tokens.
items.smallest_test: On one headless Spark with Spark Attic, run the LoRA model in SGLang with and without DSpine and measure how many parallel OpenCode sessions keep under a fixed latency. Success is at least 2x the sessions of the base setup.
items.disconfirm: DSpine's acceptance rate collapses with the LoRA loaded, or the token savings vanish on the firm's own repositories.

items.lead: Google has a new Gemini generation out, and any team comparing hosted models now has to include it.
items.body: Builders can now test Gemini 4 Neon against the model they use today. It drew 858 points and 683 comments on Hacker News, which shows wide interest. The source gives no benchmarks or pricing, so cost and quality are still open questions.

items.lead: Two small Apache 2.0 audio models together cover the front end of a private voice pipeline.
items.body: Inworld's model pulls a clean voice out of noisy audio in real time. Reson8's 0.5B model transcribes on device across 40+ languages. Together they let builders chain cleanup and transcription with no licensing friction and no cloud call. Neither is independently tested: the isolator has no published quality or latency numbers, and the 6.60 English WER comes from the model card.

items.lead: Open image-text models from RadixArk and Tencent give self-hosting teams more to try, but the evidence is thin.
items.body: RadixArk says its 27B agent model lifts Terminal-Bench 4.1 from 5.6% to 12.0%. That gain is self-reported, and the absolute score is still low. Tencent's Hy4-flash is trending with 280 likes, but the source gives no benchmarks or license details. Both are worth a quick test before anyone switches to them.
